title: Constructive complexity proof inventory
counting_unit: Labeled theorem, lemma, or corollary group; a group may contain several consequences. These are reconstructions of classical mathematics, not claims of novelty.

global_status.iPRA_reading: Explicit finite numerical representations, primitive-recursive bounds, and bounded invariants lowered to quantifier-free induction, subject to each claim's stated hypotheses.
global_status.scope: Selected results from the source article and immediate linked topics; not an exhaustive proof of every statement on every linked page.

claims.title: finite decisions and least witnesses
claims.section: The arithmetic foundation and its proof discipline
claims.statement_tex:
For every \emph{fixed} PR Boolean predicate $b(i,\vec x)$, there are PR functions
\[
 \Any_b(r,\vec x),\quad \All_b(r,\vec x),\quad \mu_b(r,\vec x)\le r
\]
such that \ipra\ proves
\begin{align*}
 \Any_b(r,\vec x)=1&\ \longleftrightarrow\ \exists i<r\ b(i,\vec x)=1,\\
 \All_b(r,\vec x)=1&\ \longleftrightarrow\ \forall i<r\ b(i,\vec x)=1.
\end{align*}
If a successful index exists, $\mu_b$ is its least value; otherwise $\mu_b=r$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Fixed primitive-recursive finite predicates and explicitly bounded searches.

claims.title: bounded formulas and bounded induction
claims.section: The arithmetic foundation and its proof discipline
claims.statement_tex: For each fixed formula $A$ whose quantifiers have PR bounds, there is a fixed PR bit $\chi_A$ and an \ipra\ proof $A\leftrightarrow\chi_A=1$. Induction for $A$ is consequently derivable from quantifier-free induction.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Bounded-formula syntax is fixed externally; this is not a total primitive-recursive evaluator for arbitrary PR syntax. Induction is lowered to quantifier-free Boolean induction.

claims.title: bounded-loop correctness
claims.section: The arithmetic foundation and its proof discipline
claims.statement_tex: Suppose a finite program has a PR fuel bound $T(\vec x)$, PR state updates, and a PR bound $B(\vec x)$ on all state codes throughout that run. If an invariant has only quantifiers bounded by explicit PR terms, its base case and preservation prove correctness in \ipra. This includes bounded least search, array dynamic programming, and a depth-first traversal of a finitely bounded tree.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Loop states, iterations, and invariant quantifiers require explicit primitive-recursive numerical bounds.

claims.title: finite counting and pigeonhole
claims.section: The arithmetic foundation and its proof discipline
claims.statement_tex: For any explicitly coded map $f:\{0,\ldots,r-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$, injectivity implies $r\le s$. If $r>s$, bounded search constructs $i<j<r$ with $f(i)=f(j)$. For any Boolean predicates $P_i$ on a finite set $X$, the size of their union is at most the sum of their sizes.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Maps and sets are finite coded data; witness extraction uses bounded search.

claims.title: bounded simulation and trace uniqueness
claims.section: The arithmetic foundation and its proof discipline
claims.statement_tex: There are fixed PR functions $\Run(e,x,t)$ and $\B(e,x,t)\in\bits$ for the configuration and acceptance bit after $t$ transitions. A correctly coded trace of length $t+1$ beginning at the initial configuration agrees with $\Run$ at every position. Accepting or rejecting output remains unchanged under additional fuel. All statements have \ipra\ proofs.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: All evaluation has an explicit clock; no unbounded halting or total universal PR evaluator is assumed.

claims.title: concrete polynomial simulation
claims.section: The arithmetic foundation and its proof discipline
claims.statement_tex: For a fixed number of source tapes, time $t$ can be simulated on one tape in $O((n+t+1)^2)$ time. There is also a fixed interpreter that, with a finite source table of length $m$ and a unary clock $t$, computes $\B(e,x,t)$ in at most $C(m+n+t+1)^4$ transitions for a fixed constant $C$. Both simulations and their bounds admit bounded-invariant \ipra\ proofs.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: The first simulation fixes the source tape count; the variable-program interpreter uses canonical fixed-alphabet source descriptions. Numeric PR operations are not treated as unit-cost machine steps.

claims.title: basic time and space inclusions
claims.section: Presentations of complexity classes and basic constructions
claims.statement_tex:
The following transformations are provable in \ipra:
\[
 \mathsf P\subseteq\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathsf{PSPACE}
 \subseteq\mathsf{EXPTIME},\qquad
 \mathsf{coNP}\subseteq\mathsf{PSPACE},
\]
and $\mathsf P\subseteq\mathsf{coNP}$. Together with the space results this gives
$\mathsf L\subseteq\mathsf{NL}\subseteq\mathsf P$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Class memberships use numerical machine/verifier presentations of specified PR language bits.

claims.title: closure constructions for P
claims.section: Presentations of complexity classes and basic constructions
claims.statement_tex: $\mathsf P$ is closed under complement, finite union, finite intersection, difference, concatenation, and Kleene star. The constructors and correctness proofs are effective in \ipra.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Finite Boolean operations and finite dynamic programming; empty-word and empty-factor cases are handled explicitly.

claims.title: positive closures of NP and coNP
claims.title_tex: positive closures of NP and coNP
claims.section: Presentations of complexity classes and basic constructions
claims.statement_tex: $\mathsf{NP}$ is closed under finite union, finite intersection, concatenation, and Kleene star. $\mathsf{coNP}$ is closed under finite union and finite intersection.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: NP complement closure is not asserted. coNP closures use complements of decidable language bits.

claims.title: encoding invariance and the function/decision distinction
claims.title_tex: encoding invariance and the function/decision distinction
claims.section: Presentations of complexity classes and basic constructions
claims.statement_tex: If two encodings have polynomial-time translations that preserve and recover the represented object, polynomial-time solvability and NP verification transfer in both directions. A polynomial-time function with polynomially long output has a polynomial-time graph predicate. A polynomial-time graph predicate alone gives a bounded-search function algorithm only when a length bound is supplied; it need not give a polynomial-time function algorithm.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: The reverse function-from-graph search needs a supplied output-length bound and need not run in polynomial time.

claims.title: unary and binary bounded-time acceptance
claims.section: Presentations of complexity classes and basic constructions
claims.statement_tex: The problem ``does deterministic $e$ accept $x$ within $T$ steps?'' is P-complete under logarithmic-space many-one reductions when $T$ is written in unary, and EXPTIME-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions when $T$ is written in binary. With nondeterministic $e$, the two versions are respectively NP-complete and NEXPTIME-complete.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Unary and binary budget encodings define different problems. Reduction resources are those explicitly stated for each completeness conclusion.

claims.title: unary and binary bounded-space acceptance
claims.section: Presentations of complexity classes and basic constructions
claims.statement_tex: Deterministic acceptance with a supplied space budget $s$, where escape or nonhalting within the configuration bound counts as rejection, is PSPACE-complete for unary $s$ and EXPSPACE-complete for binary $s$, under polynomial-time many-one reductions.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Canonical fixed-alphabet space-bounded machines; budget escape or timeout at the finite configuration bound means rejection.

claims.title: constructive algebra of reductions
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
Let $A,B,C$ be represented decision bits. If polynomial-time transducers $f,g$
satisfy $A(x)=B(f(x))$ and $B(z)=C(g(z))$, their composed transducer is a
polynomial-time reduction $A\leq_m^p C$. Identity and composition are explicit,
and polynomial-time decidability is preserved downwards. Logarithmic-space
many-one reductions have the same composition property.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Transducer resource bounds are supplied; logspace composition recomputes a virtual input rather than storing the intermediate word.

claims.title: verifier and branching presentations of NP
claims.title_tex: verifier and branching presentations of NP
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
Polynomial-time binary nondeterministic machines and polynomial-length,
polynomial-time verifiers define the same decision bits. The translations
send accepting witnesses to accepting witnesses by primitive-recursive maps.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Witness transformations establish existence equivalence, not a bijection between all padded paths and verifier strings.

claims.title: uniform finite computation circuits
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
For a fixed verifier $V$ and a supplied polynomial clock $T(n)\ge n+q(n)+1$,
there is a polynomial-time constructor $x\mapsto C_x$ with $q(n)$ input bits
such that, for every $q(n)$-bit vector $y$,
\[
 C_x(y)=V_T(x,y).
\]
There is a constant $c_V$ with at most $c_V(T(n)+1)^2$ gates and a polynomial
bit-length bound for $C_x$. The construction is logspace for fixed $V,q,T$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Verifier and polynomial clocks are fixed/supplied; the circuit printer has a separate polynomial/logspace resource analysis.

claims.title: Tseitin constraints have unique extensions
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
There is a linear-size conversion of an acyclic circuit $C$ to a 3CNF formula
$F_C$, with the original inputs retained as designated variables, such that
restriction and gate evaluation give inverse maps between satisfying
assignments of $F_C$ and inputs on which $C$ outputs one.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: An explicit variable universe retains unused inputs; unique extension includes every gate, including unused gates.

claims.title: SAT, circuit SAT, and 3SAT are NP-complete
claims.title_tex: SAT, circuit SAT, and 3SAT are NP-complete
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
Every polynomial verifier has an explicit polynomial many-one reduction to
3SAT, with primitive-recursive forward and reverse witness maps. SAT and
circuit SAT are NP-complete as well.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Completeness is obtained from supplied polynomial verifier presentations; no unknown time bound is inferred.

claims.title: circuit value is P-complete under logspace reductions
claims.title_tex: circuit value is P-complete under logspace reductions
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
The problem of evaluating an explicitly supplied acyclic Boolean circuit with
specified input bits is in P and is hard for P under logarithmic-space
many-one reductions.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Explicit acyclic circuit evaluation with given input bits; hardness uses logspace printers.

claims.title: CLIQUE is NP-complete
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
Given a 3CNF $F$ with $m$ clauses, one can construct in polynomial time a graph
$G_F$ such that $F$ is satisfiable exactly when $G_F$ has an $m$-vertex clique.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Explicit finite simple graphs and clique witnesses; empty clauses and the zero-clause case follow stated conventions.

claims.title: independent set and vertex cover are NP-complete
claims.title_tex: independent set and vertex cover are NP-complete
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
For a graph $G$ on $N$ vertices and $0\le k\le N$, the following equivalent
witness transformations are polynomial:
\[
\begin{split}
G\text{ has a }k\text{-clique}
 &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \overline G\text{ has an independent set of size }k,\\
G\text{ has an independent set of size }k
 &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ G\text{ has a vertex cover of size }N-k.
\end{split}
\]
Consequently INDEPENDENT SET and VERTEX COVER are NP-complete.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Simple graphs; the vertex-set complement transforms independent sets and vertex covers.

claims.title: a parsimonious 3SAT-to-SUBSET-SUM reduction
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
For every 3CNF on $v$ designated variables with $m$ clauses, there is a
polynomial-time binary SUBSET-SUM instance with $2v+2m$ indexed positive
integers. Satisfying assignments and subsets summing to the target are in
explicit bijection. In particular, SUBSET SUM is NP-complete.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Subsets are indexed, so equal-valued entries remain distinct. Base-eight columns avoid every carry and have unique slack completion.

claims.title: PARTITION and 0–1 KNAPSACK are NP-complete
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
SUBSET SUM has explicit polynomial reductions to PARTITION and to the
0--1 knapsack decision problem with nonnegative integer weights and profits.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Nonnegative integer SUBSET SUM/0-1 KNAPSACK inputs; zero total and out-of-range target are handled separately.

claims.title: 0–1 integer feasibility is NP-complete
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
Feasibility of a finite system of integer linear inequalities with every
variable constrained to $\{0,1\}$ is NP-complete, even for the inequalities
arising from clauses of width at most three.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Variables are constrained to 0 or 1; no unrestricted integer-programming certificate bound is claimed.

claims.title: elementary NP presentations of neighboring problems
claims.title_tex: elementary NP presentations of neighboring problems
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
Graph isomorphism, Hamiltonian path, Hamiltonian cycle, and the bounded-factor
problem have explicit polynomial verifiers. The latter asks, on $N\ge2$,
whether $N$ has a divisor $d$ with $2\le d\le b$ and $d<N$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Only elementary NP membership is proved for the listed problems. No Hamiltonian hardness, polynomial factoring algorithm, coNP factoring certificate, or graph-isomorphism speed bound is inferred.

claims.title: constructive 2SAT criterion and polynomial algorithm
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
A 2CNF formula without empty clauses is satisfiable if and only if no variable
and its complement are mutually reachable in its implication graph. There is
a polynomial algorithm returning either a satisfying assignment or a
variable together with the two contradictory implication paths.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: 2CNF with explicit variable universe; the displayed polynomial implementation materializes reachability and is not claimed to use logarithmic workspace.

claims.title: Horn satisfiability has a least-model algorithm
claims.title_tex: Horn satisfiability has a least-model algorithm
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
Satisfiability of CNF formulas with at most one positive literal per clause is
polynomial-time decidable. On satisfiable input an explicit algorithm returns
the coordinatewise least satisfying assignment.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Horn clauses have at most one positive literal; the algorithm computes the least model when one exists.

claims.title: constructive SAT search-to-decision
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
A supplied polynomial-time SAT decider yields a polynomial-time algorithm
which returns a satisfying assignment for any satisfiable formula and returns
``none'' for an unsatisfiable one. The same supplied decider yields such a
search algorithm for every polynomial verifier presentation.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Conditional on a supplied polynomial-time SAT decider; the result is a total witness finder with a distinguished failure output.

claims.title: the constructive completeness implication
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
A polynomial SAT decider implies a polynomial decider and a polynomial witness
finder for every presented NP problem. Conversely, if every NP presentation
has a polynomial decider, SAT does. Thus the standard statement
$\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$ is equivalent to $\mathrm{SAT}\in\mathrm P$ under the
numerical class-presentation convention of this report.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Equivalence/conditional compiler theorem only; neither P=NP nor P≠NP is established.

claims.title: an NP-complete coNP problem collapses NP and coNP
claims.title_tex: an NP-complete coNP problem collapses NP and coNP
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
If a supplied NP-complete problem $K$ also has a coNP presentation, then
$\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{coNP}$. In particular, $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$ implies
$\mathrm{NP}=\mathrm{coNP}$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Conditional on a supplied NP-complete coNP presentation (or P=NP); the hypothesis is not asserted.

claims.title: parsimonious completeness for witness counting
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
For the counting convention
\[
 f_V(x)=\sum_{y<2^{q(|x|)}} [V_T(x,y)=1],
\]
counting satisfying assignments of circuits and of 3CNF formulas is
\#$\mathrm P$-complete under parsimonious polynomial many-one reductions.
Counting indexed subsets of a positive integer list with a specified sum is
also \#$\mathrm P$-complete under those reductions.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: #P uses exact declared witness lengths. Completeness is parsimonious for the specified circuit, 3CNF, and indexed-subset conventions.

claims.title: a factor-two vertex-cover approximation
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
There is a polynomial algorithm that returns a vertex cover $C$ satisfying
$|C|\le2|C^*|$ for every vertex cover $C^*$ of the same graph.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Factor-two approximation; no optimum-computation claim.

claims.title: vertex cover is fixed-parameter tractable
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
For a graph on $N$ vertices and parameter $k$, vertex cover of size at most
$k$ can be decided, and a cover produced, in time
$2^{k+1}\poly(N+|E|+1)$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Time is exponential in parameter k and polynomial in the remaining explicit graph size.

claims.title: UNSAT and tautology are coNP-complete
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
UNSAT, propositional TAUT, and tautology for DNF formulas with terms of width
at most three are coNP-complete under polynomial many-one reductions.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: UNSAT/TAUT use finite Boolean complements; no unbounded double-negation elimination is used.

claims.title: Horn SAT is P-complete under logspace reductions
claims.title_tex: Horn SAT is P-complete under logspace reductions
claims.section: Reductions, complete problems, and constructive search
claims.statement_tex:
Horn satisfiability is P-complete, even when every clause has width at most
three. The hardness reduction uses only finite gate-local rules.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Dual-rail Horn construction; exactly-one-rail holds for the least closure, not necessarily for every Horn model.

claims.title: bounded reachability and constructive path shortening
claims.title_tex: bounded reachability and constructive path shortening
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
The bit $r_i(v)$ is one exactly when a walk from $a$ to $v$ of length at
most $i$ exists.  A witnessing walk can be obtained by primitive recursion
and bounded search.  Every walk in an $N$-vertex graph has a walk with the
same endpoints and length at most $N-1$.  Thus $r_{N-1}=r_N$, and their
common value decides unrestricted finite-walk reachability.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Finite graphs with explicit vertex/code bounds; path witnesses are constructed by bounded operations.

claims.title: the finite configuration theorem
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
Acceptance within the supplied space budget is equivalent to reachability
of the accepting sink in the above graph, and hence to existence of a
computation of fewer than $N$ transitions in that graph.  The
configuration graph and its edge test are primitive-recursive.  For
$s\geq\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil$, its vertices and edge test use $O(s)$
working bits.  A deterministic computation which eventually halts has
halted before repeating an ordinary configuration.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Read-only input; a supplied finite work budget defines the configuration graph. The O(s) record bound uses s at least the logarithmic input-length bound.

claims.title: directed reachability is NL-complete
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
Directed graph reachability is complete for $\mathrm{NL}$ under
logarithmic-space many-one reductions.  In particular,
\[
 \mathrm L\subseteq\mathrm{NL}\subseteq\mathrm P.
\]
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Explicit directed graphs and logarithmic-space many-one reductions.

claims.title: even acyclic directed reachability is NL-complete
claims.title_tex: even acyclic directed reachability is NL-complete
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
The restriction of directed reachability to directed acyclic graphs is
NL-complete, by a logarithmic-space reduction whose correctness has
explicit path maps.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Layered construction gives an acyclic directed graph; graph size remains polynomial.

claims.title: Savitch's finite theorem
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
The bit $R_j(a,b)$ is one exactly when there is a walk from $a$ to $b$
of length at most $2^j$.  There is a deterministic implementation of
$R_j(a,b)$ using
\[
 O\bigl((j+1)(\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil+
                    \lceil\log_2(j+2)\rceil)+w\bigr)
 \tag{S.5}
\]
working bits when the edge test uses $w$ working bits.  Its time is
bounded by an explicit primitive-recursive function; for a polynomial-time
edge test one may use
$C(2N+2)^{j+2}(\ell+j+2)^C$ with a suitable fixed $C$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Primitive-recursive whole-table definability is separated from the depth-first small-space implementation; the edge-access resource is accounted for.

claims.title: the principal space equalities
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
For the explicit budget conventions above and $s(n)\geq\log_2(n+2)$,
\[
 \mathrm{NSPACE}(s)\subseteq\mathrm{DSPACE}(s^2).
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathrm{NL}\subseteq\mathrm{DSPACE}(\log^2 n),\qquad
 \mathrm{NPSPACE}=\mathrm{PSPACE},\\
 \mathrm{NEXPSPACE}=\mathrm{EXPSPACE},\qquad
 \mathrm{PSPACE}\subseteq\mathrm{EXPTIME}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: General resource substitution uses s(n) at least logarithmic and a supplied O(s(n))-space budget constructor, as stipulated in the space section. Standard logarithmic, polynomial, and exponential budgets qualify.

claims.title: forced enumeration
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
Suppose the exact number $c_i$ is supplied.  There is a nondeterministic
$O(\log(N+2))$-space procedure which, on a requested $v$, certifies
$v\notin A_{i+1}$.  Every completed successful branch certifies that
fact, and if the fact holds a successful branch can be constructed by a
primitive-recursive procedure.  Here $0\leq i<N$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: The exact reachable-vertex count is supplied; successful branches certify every selected path and cannot merely guess nonmembership.

claims.title: constructive space complementation
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
Nonreachability has a nondeterministic logarithmic-space recognizer whose
accepting transcripts are sound and whose successful transcript can be
constructed primitively recursively whenever nonreachability holds.
For the budgeted machine presentations above,
\[
 \mathrm{NSPACE}(s)=\mathrm{coNSPACE}(s)
 \quad(s\geq\log_2(n+2)),
 \qquad \mathrm{NL}=\mathrm{coNL}.
\]
These classes are closed under finite unions, intersections, differences,
and symmetric differences.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: General NSPACE complementation assumes s(n) at least logarithmic and a supplied O(s(n))-space budget constructor, or uses an explicit budget parameter.

claims.title: 2SAT is NL-complete
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
Satisfiability of formulae with clauses of size at most two is
NL-complete under logarithmic-space reductions.  Its restriction to
clauses of the forms $\neg x_u\vee x_v$ and unit clauses is already
NL-hard.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Uses the constructive 2SAT criterion and NL=coNL; empty/invalid syntax conventions are handled explicitly.

claims.title: bounded evaluation of QBF
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
There is a primitive-recursive evaluator for closed Boolean formulae,
and a deterministic polynomial-space implementation.  Truth has an
explicit finite winning strategy for existential choices; falsity has
an explicit finite counterstrategy for universal choices.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: QBF has finite explicit syntax and finite Boolean quantifiers; syntax evaluation is distinct from arbitrary first-order truth.

claims.title: polynomial-size quantified reachability
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
For all endpoint assignments, $\Theta_j(U,V)$ has value $R_j(U,V)$.
Its syntax has one copy of $D_x$ and only $O(j\ell)$ extra connective
and variable occurrences.  With binary variable indices its encoded
length is bounded by
\[
 O\bigl((|D_x|+j\ell)\log((j+1)\ell+2)\bigr),
 \tag{S.9}
\]
where $|D_x|$ counts syntax nodes before variable-name encoding.  Construction,
renaming, and substitution of constant endpoints take polynomial time
in the output bound.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: A single recursive formula occurrence and fresh variables give polynomial syntax size; exponential path unrolling is avoided.

claims.title: TQBF is PSPACE-complete
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
Every fixed polynomial-space machine presentation has a polynomial-time
many-one reduction to TQBF, with an iPRA proof of its numerical
correctness equation.  Together with S10 this proves PSPACE completeness.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Polynomial-space source deciders have supplied budgets; the complete quantified syntax printer is part of the construction.

claims.title: finite strategies and game completeness
claims.section: Space, reachability, complementation, and finite games
claims.statement_tex:
The winner of a supplied game is decided by a primitive-recursive
Boolean function.  One of the players has a canonical finite winning
strategy.  Deciding whether the existential player wins is PSPACE-complete
under polynomial-time reductions.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Finite polynomial-horizon/succinctly represented games under the stated encoding; no unrestricted infinite-game determinacy is claimed.

claims.title: P is properly contained in EXPTIME
claims.title_tex: P is properly contained in EXPTIME
claims.section: Explicit separation witnesses and coarse hierarchies
claims.statement_tex:
There is a fixed PR bit $D$ computed by a fixed machine in time $2^{K(n+1)^2}$, for a fixed constant $K$, such that \ipra\ proves, uniformly in $e,c\ge1,k$,
\[
 D(W(e,c,k))\ne
 \B\bigl(e,W(e,c,k),c(|W(e,c,k)|+1)^k\bigr).
\]
Consequently no polynomial-time presentation decides $D$, and $\mathsf P\subsetneq\mathsf{EXPTIME}$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: An explicit mismatch word excludes every polynomial descriptor; this does not separate P from NP.

claims.title: a coarse fixed-degree time hierarchy
claims.section: Explicit separation witnesses and coarse hierarchies
claims.statement_tex:
For every fixed integer $k\ge1$, on the canonical model with read-only input and one work tape,
\[
 \mathsf{DTIME}_{\mathrm{can}}((n+1)^k)
 \subsetneq
 \mathsf{DTIME}_{\mathrm{can}}((n+1)^{4k+4}).
\]
There is a PR counterexample word for each proposed machine and constant in the lower class.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Canonical one-tape model and the displayed coarse exponent gap; not the sharp deterministic time-hierarchy theorem.

claims.title: L is properly contained in PSPACE
claims.title_tex: L is properly contained in PSPACE
claims.section: Explicit separation witnesses and coarse hierarchies
claims.statement_tex: There is a PR language $D_{\log}$ in PSPACE and a PR map $W$ such that every logarithmic-space descriptor $(e,c)$ disagrees with $D_{\log}$ on $W(e,c,0)$. Thus $\mathsf L\subsetneq\mathsf{PSPACE}$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Fixed-machine constant-factor space normalization and explicit padded descriptors; this is a concrete large-gap separation.

claims.title: PSPACE is properly contained in EXPSPACE
claims.title_tex: PSPACE is properly contained in EXPSPACE
claims.section: Explicit separation witnesses and coarse hierarchies
claims.statement_tex: There is a PR language $D_{\mathrm{ps}}$ in EXPSPACE with a PR disagreement input for every polynomial-space descriptor. In particular $\mathsf{PSPACE}\subsetneq\mathsf{EXPSPACE}$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Explicit polynomial/exponential space envelopes; no general sharp space-hierarchy theorem is asserted.

claims.title: an exponential-time hierarchy step
claims.section: Explicit separation witnesses and coarse hierarchies
claims.statement_tex: Let $2\mathsf{EXPTIME}$ denote the union of deterministic time classes with clocks $2^{2^{p(n)}}$ for polynomials $p$. There is an explicit PR language in $2\mathsf{EXPTIME}$ outside EXPTIME, with PR counterexample inputs for all exponential-time descriptors. Hence $\mathsf{EXPTIME}\subsetneq2\mathsf{EXPTIME}$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: The displayed coarse exponential-time hierarchy step only; arbitrary sharp hierarchy/constructibility hypotheses are not silently assumed.

claims.title: alternating polynomial time equals polynomial space
claims.title_tex: alternating polynomial time equals polynomial space
claims.section: Alternation, the polynomial hierarchy, and parallel circuits
claims.statement_tex: For clocked finite presentations, $\mathsf{AP}=\mathsf{PSPACE}$, with descriptor transformations and \ipra\ proofs of equality of acceptance bits.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Clocked finite alternation; AP means alternating polynomial time. Infinite strategies are not quantified over.

claims.title: duality, monotonicity, and the space bound for PH
claims.title_tex: duality, monotonicity, and the space bound for PH
claims.section: Alternation, the polynomial hierarchy, and parallel circuits
claims.statement_tex: For every fixed $k$, complementation interchanges $\Sigma_k^{\mathsf P}$ and $\Pi_k^{\mathsf P}$. Each level is included in both appropriately prefixed next levels, and all finite levels are contained in PSPACE. In particular $\Sigma_1^{\mathsf P}=\mathsf{NP}$ and $\Pi_1^{\mathsf P}=\mathsf{coNP}$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: One result for each fixed finite PH level; the union PH is metatheoretic terminology, not an unrestricted internal induction on semantic classes.

claims.title: bounded-alternation QBF completeness
claims.section: Alternation, the polynomial hierarchy, and parallel circuits
claims.statement_tex: For each fixed $k\ge1$, truth of polynomial-size quantified Boolean formulas with $k$ alternating blocks beginning existentially is $\Sigma_k^{\mathsf P}$-complete under polynomial many-one reductions. The universally beginning version is $\Pi_k^{\mathsf P}$-complete. The quantifier-free matrix may be an arbitrary Boolean formula; no restricted CNF claim is needed.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Fixed number of alternating blocks. The matrix may be an arbitrary Boolean formula; no same-block restricted-CNF claim is made. Gate variables join the last block.

claims.title: conditional collapses, stated constructively
claims.section: Alternation, the polynomial hierarchy, and parallel circuits
claims.statement_tex: For each fixed $k$, the numerical hypothesis $\mathsf P=\mathsf{NP}$ implies $\Sigma_k^{\mathsf P}=\Pi_k^{\mathsf P}=\mathsf P$. The hypothesis $\mathsf{NP}=\mathsf{coNP}$ implies $\Sigma_k^{\mathsf P}=\Pi_k^{\mathsf P}=\mathsf{NP}$ for $k\ge1$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Conditional collapses at every fixed finite level. Neither equality hypothesis is asserted, and bare existential class equality is not replaced by a global PR choice function.

claims.title: balancing and sequential simulation
claims.section: Alternation, the polynomial hierarchy, and parallel circuits
claims.statement_tex:
For every fixed $k\ge0$,
\[
 \mathsf{NC}^k\subseteq\mathsf{AC}^k\subseteq\mathsf{NC}^{k+1},
 \qquad \mathsf{NC}=\mathsf{AC}\subseteq\mathsf P,
\]
where NC and AC denote their finite-level unions with the uniformity convention above.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Logspace-uniform polynomial-size circuit families and the stated fan-in conventions; finite unions NC and AC are metatheoretic.

claims.title: shallow uniform circuits use logarithmic space
claims.title_tex: shallow uniform circuits use logarithmic space
claims.section: Alternation, the polynomial hierarchy, and parallel circuits
claims.statement_tex: $\mathsf{NC}^1\subseteq\mathsf L$. More generally, a uniform bounded-fan-in circuit of depth $d(n)$ and polynomial size can be evaluated using $O(d(n)+\ell(n))$ work space, with a PR time bound when $d$ has one.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Logspace-uniform bounded-fan-in polynomial-size circuits. Gate replay yields O(depth+log size) storage; general evaluation time may be superpolynomial.

claims.title: NL has uniform quadratic-logarithmic-depth circuits
claims.section: Alternation, the polynomial hierarchy, and parallel circuits
claims.statement_tex:
$\mathsf{NL}\subseteq\mathsf{NC}^2$. Consequently
\[
 \mathsf{NC}^1\subseteq\mathsf L\subseteq\mathsf{NL}
 \subseteq\mathsf{NC}^2\subseteq\mathsf P.
\]
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Uniform NC^2 construction uses explicit circuit adjacency tests and balanced Boolean matrix squaring; it does not rely on an arbitrary logspace reduction preserving depth.

claims.title: finite counting calculus
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
The following statements have primitive-recursive witnesses and proofs by
quantifier-free induction in the bounded compilation described earlier.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $0\leq C_E(N)\leq N$, and $C_E(N)>0$ if and only if there is an
      $i<N$ with $E(i)=1$. If the count is positive, the least such $i$ is
      obtained by a bounded scan.
\item If $E(i)\leq F(i)$ for all $i<N$, then $C_E(N)\leq C_F(N)$.
      For a finite family $(E_j)_{j<k}$,
      $|\bigcup_{j<k}E_j|\leq\sum_{j<k}|E_j|$.
\item $|E\times F|=|E||F|$. More generally, a sum of products over a
      finite Cartesian product factors into the product of the sums.
\item If a permutation of $[0,N)$ carries $E$ onto $F$, their counts agree.
      If an explicitly described involution without fixed points exchanges
      $E$ and its complement, then $2|E|=N$.
\item If $|E|<N$, the least $i<N$ outside $E$ exists and is found by bounded
      search. The same assertion applies to a union whose displayed upper
      bound is strictly below $N$.
\end{enumerate}
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Finite counts and bounded tables; missing elements and positive-count witnesses are found by bounded search.

claims.title: one-sided randomness and witnesses
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
$\mathrm{P}\subseteq\mathrm{RP}\subseteq\mathrm{NP}$ and
$\mathrm{P}\subseteq\mathrm{coRP}\subseteq\mathrm{coNP}$.
An RP computation repeated independently $k\geq1$ times, accepting if any
trial accepts, still has no false positives and has at most $Q^k/2^k$
false-negative seeds. The analogous AND construction amplifies coRP.
In particular RP and coRP are contained in BPP.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Fixed finite seed cubes and positive language-bit correctness specifications; independence is finite product counting.

claims.title: integer BPP amplification
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
For every $d\geq1$, taking the majority of $12d$ independent BPP trials
(breaking ties in a fixed way) gives
\[
 2^d e_{\mathrm{amp},L}(x)<Q(n)^{12d}.
\]
The number of random bits is $12d\,r(n)$; if $d$ is polynomial in $n$,
the amplified machine is polynomial time.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Exact integer amplification inequalities; polynomial-time amplification requires a polynomial repetition parameter.

claims.title: elementary closure of randomized classes
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
BPP is closed under complement, union, intersection, and polynomial-time
many-one preimages. RP and coRP are each closed under union, intersection,
and polynomial-time many-one preimages.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Randomized programs have explicit polynomial clocks and seed bounds.

claims.title: algebra of witness counts
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
$\#\mathrm P$ is closed under addition, multiplication, and polynomially
bounded sums of uniformly polynomial-time verifiers. Its positive supports
are precisely NP. Every nonnegative polynomial-time computable function
of polynomial output length is a $\#\mathrm P$ function. A fixed
presentation $f(x)=\#\{w<2^{p(n)}:V(x,w)=1\}$ also gives a
$\#\mathrm P$ presentation of $2^{p(n)}-f(x)$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Exact witness lengths with canonical zero padding; complement counts are relative to a specified witness cube, not arbitrary subtraction closure.

claims.title: PP containments and complement
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
$\mathrm{NP}\cup\mathrm{coNP}\cup\mathrm{BPP}\subseteq\mathrm{PP}
\subseteq\mathrm{PSPACE}$, and PP is closed under complement. Every
$\#\mathrm P$ function is computable using polynomial work space and
exponential time.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: PP uses strict majority; the complement construction corrects ties explicitly. Exact counting may require exponential time.

claims.title: BPP has polynomial advice and circuits
claims.title_tex: BPP has polynomial advice and circuits
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
From a BPP presentation one can construct, for every length $n$, a
polynomial-length advice string $a_n$ that makes a fixed polynomial-time
machine correct on all $n$-bit inputs. The function $n\mapsto a_n$ can be
chosen primitive recursively. Consequently
$\mathrm{BPP}\subseteq\mathrm P/\mathrm{poly}$ in the finite circuit
and advice readings.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Advice can be chosen PR from the supplied BPP presentation, but no polynomial-time advice construction is claimed. Arbitrary P/poly languages need not be recursive.

claims.title: the translate-covering construction
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
Every BPP presentation has both a $\Sigma^\mathrm P_2$ presentation and a
$\Pi^\mathrm P_2$ presentation, with explicit polynomial bounds and
primitive-recursive witness searches. Hence
\[
 \mathrm{BPP}\subseteq\Sigma^\mathrm P_2\cap\Pi^\mathrm P_2.
\]
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Positive finite Sigma_2 and Pi_2 presentations with polynomial block lengths; all covering searches have explicit finite bounds.

claims.title: zero-error equivalence and restart bounds
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
The following presentations are interconvertible by explicit machine
constructions: (i) a bounded zero-error trial of success density at least
one half; (ii) an RP presentation and a coRP presentation of the same
Boolean language; (iii) a trace-sound random machine with a polynomial
finite expected-time certificate (R9). Thus the finite arithmetical
reading of $\mathrm{ZPP}=\mathrm{RP}\cap\mathrm{coRP}$ is provable in
\ipra. Repeating (i) for at most $j$ rounds leaves failure density at most
$2^{-j}$, and its average number of rounds is at most two for every cap.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Expected time means the stated inequalities for all finite truncation caps, together with trace soundness. Termination on every infinite random tape is not asserted.

claims.title: quantitative circuit counting
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
The number of $n$-input Boolean functions computable with at most $s$ gates
is at most
\[
 B(n,s)=(n+s+2)\bigl(16(n+s+2)^2\bigr)^s.
\]
If $B(n,s)<2^{2^n}$, a primitive-recursive bounded search produces a truth
table not computed by any such circuit.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Fixed finite complete gate basis; description counting allows collisions and invalid descriptions only in an upper bound.

claims.title: a concrete Shannon bound
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
For $n\geq4$ let
\[
 s(n)=\left\lfloor\frac{2^n}{16(n+1)}\right\rfloor.
\]
At most $2^{2^{n-1}}$ truth tables on $n$ bits have circuits of size at most
$s(n)$. In particular a least hard table $h_n$ exists, and at least
$2^{2^n}-2^{2^{n-1}}$ tables require more gates.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: The explicit numerical bound is stated for n>=4 and the supplied circuit encoding.

claims.title: a primitive-recursive language outside polynomial circuits
claims.title_tex: a primitive-recursive language outside polynomial circuits
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
There is a primitive-recursive Boolean language $H$, decidable in
space $2^{O(n)}$, with no polynomial-size circuit family. For every
$c\geq1$ and $k\geq0$, the explicitly chosen length
\[
 n=2^{4(k+c+4)}
\]
has the property that no circuit with at most $c(n+1)^k$ gates computes
$H$ correctly on all inputs of that length. For each such circuit a least
mismatch input is primitive recursively obtainable.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: An explicit PR language in exponential space lies outside polynomial circuits. No reverse containment for unrestricted nonuniform advice is asserted.

claims.title: a constructive universal circuit upper bound
claims.title_tex: a constructive universal circuit upper bound
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
Every truth table on $n\geq1$ inputs has a circuit with at most
$n2^n+n$ gates, constructed primitive recursively from the table.
For $n\geq64$ there is a compiler producing a circuit $C$ with
\[
 n\,\operatorname{size}(C)\leq18\cdot2^n.
\]
Together with Theorem~\ref{thm:R11}, this gives the order
$\Theta(2^n/n)$ for the maximum, over truth tables of length $2^n$, of
minimum circuit size. No real asymptotic expression is needed for its
integer formulation.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: The refined 18*2^n/n bound is for n>=64. The uniform compiler takes an explicit exponentially long truth table.

claims.title: finite tree capacity
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
A binary tree of depth at most $h$ has at most $2^h$ leaves. An arbitrary
finite binary tree has at most $2^h-1$ leaves at depth strictly below $h$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Finite binary trees with the stated depth convention.

claims.title: comparison sorting requires many comparisons
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
Any comparison tree that correctly sorts $n$ distinct keys has worst-case
depth $h$ satisfying
\[
 2^h\geq n!.
\]
If $n\geq4$, $a=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, and
$\ell=\lfloor\log_2 a\rfloor$, then $h\geq a\ell$.
Under the uniform distribution on the $n!$ rank orders, the average
comparison count is also $\Omega(n\log n)$ in an explicit integer form:
for every $j$ with $2^j\leq n!/2$,
\[
 2\sum_{\pi}\operatorname{depth}(\pi)\geq j\,n!.
\]
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Comparison sorting of distinct keys; average-case statement uses the uniform distribution on rank orders. No lower bound for arbitrary integer-key operations is inferred.

claims.title: exact deterministic query bounds
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
The deterministic query complexity of $n$-bit OR, AND, and parity is $n$.
For parity, every correctly answered input path must query all $n$ bits.
For OR the all-zero path must query all bits, and for AND the all-one
path must do so.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Deterministic bit-query model with exact answers.

claims.title: finite randomized query lower bounds
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
Suppose a randomized query algorithm uses a fixed finite uniform seed
space and at most $q$ queries on every input and seed, and errs on at
most one third of seeds for every input. For $n$-bit OR, $3q\geq n$.
For $n$-bit parity, $q\geq n$. The same parity conclusion applies to any
error bound strictly below one half.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: A fixed finite uniform seed space and a worst-case query cap for every input and seed, not merely an expected-query bound.

claims.title: rectangles and fooling sets
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
For each protocol leaf the input pairs reaching it form a Cartesian
product $X_0\times Y_0$. If a Boolean communication problem has a finite
set $F$ of one-inputs such that two distinct $(x,y),(x',y')\in F$ have
at least one zero cross-input $(x,y')$ or $(x',y)$, then every correct
protocol has at least $|F|$ one-leaves, and $2^h\geq|F|$ for its cost $h$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Finite deterministic protocols with shared leaf outputs; sets are finite rectangles.

claims.title: deterministic equality needs n+1 bits
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
For $n\geq1$, equality of two $n$-bit strings has deterministic
communication complexity exactly $n+1$ under the shared leaf-output
convention.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Exact n+1 bound assumes n>=1 and both participants receive the shared leaf output. Bob-only output has the separately noted n-bit bound.

claims.title: a constant-communication public-randomness equality test
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
With $kn$ shared random bits, equality has a protocol communicating
$k+1$ bits, having no false negatives and false-positive density exactly
$2^{-k}$ on unequal inputs. In particular three communicated bits suffice
for error at most one third, independently of $n$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Public randomness is explicit; the theorem does not claim the same bound with private coins.

claims.title: best, weighted average, and worst cost
claims.title_tex: best, weighted average, and worst cost
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
Let $c_0,\ldots,c_{N-1}$ be natural costs with $N>0$, and let
$w_0,\ldots,w_{N-1}$ be natural weights of total $W>0$. If
$b=\min_i c_i$ and $z=\max_i c_i$, then
\[
 bW\leq\sum_{i<N}w_ic_i\leq zW.
\]
Both extrema and the weighted sum are primitive recursive on the coded
finite lists. These inequalities give best $\leq$ weighted average
$\leq$ worst after rational interpretation.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Finite nonnegative costs and weights of positive total; amortized costs are not placed in this pointwise distributional ordering.

claims.title: the potential method over natural numbers
claims.title_tex: the potential method over natural numbers
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
For a finite state sequence $s_0,\ldots,s_m$, let $c_i$ be the cost of
the transition $s_i\to s_{i+1}$, and let $\Phi(s)$ be a nonnegative
integer potential. If
\[
 c_i+\Phi(s_{i+1})\leq a_i+\Phi(s_i)\qquad(i<m),
\]
then
\[
 \sum_{i<m}c_i+\Phi(s_m)
 \leq\sum_{i<m}a_i+\Phi(s_0).
\]
In particular $\sum_{i<m}c_i\leq\sum_{i<m}a_i+\Phi(s_0)$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Finite valid state sequences with nonnegative integer potentials.

claims.title: binary counters have constant amortized bit-flip cost
claims.title_tex: binary counters have constant amortized bit-flip cost
claims.section: Finite randomness, counting, circuits, and lower bounds
claims.statement_tex:
Starting at zero, $m$ increments of an unbounded binary counter use at
most $2m$ bit flips. More precisely, if $\nu(m)$ is the number of one bits
in the final counter, the total number of flips is $2m-\nu(m)$.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Bit-flip cost only; tape-head motion and other implementation costs require separate accounting.

claims.title: exact path-sum identity
claims.section: A finite arithmetic treatment of a quantum gate model
claims.statement_tex:
Let a circuit contain $h$ Hadamard gates. For each $u\in\bits^h$, simulate the classical reversible gates and use $u_i$ as the chosen output at the $i$th Hadamard. Let $y(u)$ be the final basis word and let $\sigma(u)\in\{1,-1\}$ be the product of its Hadamard signs. Define
\[
 s_y=\sum_{u<2^h}[y(u)=y]\,\sigma(u),\qquad
 A=\sum_{y:\,y_{\rm out}=1}s_y^2.
\]
Then the exact acceptance probability is $A/2^h$, and $\sum_y s_y^2=2^h$. These identities, including $0\le A\le2^h$, have finite \ipra\ proofs without introducing square roots as arithmetic objects.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Exact uniform Hadamard/NOT/Toffoli gate model with basis input and zero ancillas. Signed path counts encode the probabilities without real-number objects.

claims.title: classical random computation embeds exactly
claims.section: A finite arithmetic treatment of a quantum gate model
claims.statement_tex: $\mathsf{BPP}\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}_{HT}$, and in particular $\mathsf P\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}_{HT}$. The reduction preserves each input's exact rational acceptance probability.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Containment is in the explicitly defined BQP_HT class. Random seed registers are retained, so distinct seeds do not interfere.

claims.title: a PP simulation by an explicit branch gap
claims.title_tex: a PP simulation by an explicit branch gap
claims.section: A finite arithmetic treatment of a quantum gate model
claims.statement_tex: $\mathsf{BQP}_{HT}\subseteq\mathsf{PP}$, in the exact finite-majority definition of PP used in the counting section.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: PP containment is proved for the finite H/X/Toffoli model and its positive bounded-error promise; no arbitrary gate-set universality or real-amplitude theorem is imported.

claims.title: exact simulation in polynomial space
claims.section: A finite arithmetic treatment of a quantum gate model
claims.statement_tex: A polynomial-size $HT$ circuit's integer numerator $A$ and the comparison $2A>2^h$ can be computed in polynomial space. Consequently $\mathsf{BQP}_{HT}\subseteq\mathsf{PSPACE}$ independently of the PP containment.
claims.outline_coverage_note: Partial finite definitions and explicit remaining proof obligations; not a claim that this theorem is implemented or checked.
qualifications: Exact polynomial-space simulation for the stated H/X/Toffoli circuits, with exponential time. General quantum-model equivalence is not proved.
